turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's not waste them. My son found out he got a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Thanks for coming. Your son cheated. The AI checker says 94 percent, so it's settled.

Ninety-four percent is a machine's guess, and the company that sells that checker says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student. So what else do you have? And you still haven't told me who decided before anyone called me.
I don't need to show you anything else. The software is the school's software. Owen used ChatGPT, everyone knows it, and honestly kids like him always do.
"Kids like him" is not evidence. Owen's essay is the only thing on the table, so show me what you have on it. Who entered the zero, and when?
You're a lawyer so you'll want to argue, but the zero stands and there's nothing to discuss. If you want to save him, get him to confess.

"Get him to confess." Owen has told me he didn't use it, and I believe him. Nobody confesses to something they didn't do. I'm writing that down. Now answer the question: when was the zero entered, and did anyone speak to Owen before it was?
I entered the zero when I felt like it. Calling home isn't my job, you can talk to the office.

"When I felt like it." Okay. That's the admission I needed. Your own school's procedure, 4.2, says the parent is contacted before any mark consequence is entered. You didn't do that, and Owen found out on his phone in the middle of class. I'm going to the principal's office from here unless you withdraw the zero today.
Fine, here's evidence: his writing is too good. A kid who gets 62 doesn't write like that. Case closed.

"Too good." That's an opinion about his writing, and an opinion isn't a document. A kid's mark on one assignment doesn't tell you what he wrote in it. Do you have a dated draft, an earlier sample, anything with a timestamp on it? Show me that, or the zero stays under review.
Your daughter Claire had a case here too, so honestly it runs in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence. My daughter's case is not on the table. Owen's essay is. Withdraw the zero, or I'm going to the principal's office now.
Look, I'm the teacher and my word is the standard. Either he takes the zero or I take it to the principal and it goes on his file.

"Your word is the standard." Okay. Then put that in writing, and I'll put in writing that you said it. Under your own procedure, 4.4, a first concern gets a supervised reassessment, and if it shows the learning, nothing goes on his record. Owen's file is not your decision to threaten. So: is anything on his record right now?
Nothing's on his record yet, but I'll put whatever I want there. You're being emotional, calm down.

"Emotional." I'm not. I'm a litigator and I've read your procedure. You just said nothing is on his record yet, and you want to put something there without a document. Put it in an email yourself, with the basis for it. Until then, my position is this: the zero is withdrawn, Owen gets a supervised reassessment, and nothing goes on file. Yes or no?
Okay okay. Look, the real reason I'm sure: the checker, plus I just know. Will you drop it if I say sorry?

"'I just know.'" That isn't evidence, and an apology doesn't change the record. Sorry is not the zero coming off. Withdraw the zero, offer a supervised reassessment in private, and put "nothing goes on file" in writing. I'll take that, and I'll write it down exactly as you say it. Otherwise I'm going to the principal. Which is it?
Fine. Sorry. Now agree he did it and we can move on.

Sorry is not an agreement that he did it, and I won't say that about my son. I'm writing down that you apologised, and I'm writing down that you still haven't withdrawn the zero. Two things, in writing, by end of day: the zero comes off, and the reassessment is private with nothing on his file. Send it to me in an email. Otherwise I'm going upstairs.
